agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory lead)
payload: 805 kg at launch (487 kg dry) — X-ray/gamma-ray spectrometer, near-infrared spectrograph, multispectral camera, laser rangefinder (LIDAR), magnetometer. First spacecraft to orbit and land on an asteroid.
credit: © NASA / Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory — public domain. NEAR Shoemaker (Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous) launched 1996-02-17 from Cape Canaveral on the first of NASA's Discovery-program planetary missions. After an Earth gravity assist (1998-01-23) and a flyby of asteroid 253 Mathilde (1997-06-27), the spacecraft entered orbit around 433 Eros on 2000-02-14 — the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid. Over 12 months of orbital science it returned 160,000+ images and detailed spectral, compositional, and gravitational maps of the S-type chondrite body (~34 km × 11 km × 11 km). On 2001-02-12, after five orbit-lowering burns, NEAR Shoemaker executed a controlled descent at ~1.7 m/s and soft-landed on Eros near the saddle region, returning images to within 125 m of the surface — the first soft landing on any small body in the solar system. The spacecraft survived impact and continued transmitting for ~16 days from the surface.

events.label: Launch — Delta II
events.description: Cape Canaveral, 1996-02-17. First Discovery-program planetary mission. The spacecraft carried five science instruments to perform the first orbital survey of an asteroid.

events.label: 253 Mathilde — flyby
events.description: 1997-06-27: NEAR flew within 1,212 km of carbonaceous asteroid 253 Mathilde, returning 500 images of the 50 km body. Largest cratered object ever imaged relative to its size — five craters wider than the object's radius.

events.label: Earth — gravity assist
events.description: 1998-01-23: 540 km Earth flyby, raising the aphelion to match Eros's orbit. The spacecraft was briefly lost due to a thruster anomaly during a deep-space manoeuvre two weeks earlier — recovered via the Earth flyby geometry.

events.label: Eros orbit insertion
events.description: 2000-02-14: 916 km orbital insertion burn into a 200 × 366 km elliptical orbit around Eros — the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid. Over 12 months, orbit altitude was steadily reduced to build a 35 km near-circular mapping orbit.

events.label: Eros landing — EDL
events.description: 2001-02-12: five orbit-lowering burns reduced altitude to ~5 km; the final controlled descent proceeded at ~1.7 m/s. NEAR Shoemaker soft-landed near the Himeros saddle region at 35.0°N, 280.0°W, returning images from 125 m altitude. First soft landing on any small body. The spacecraft survived and transmitted from the surface for ~16 days.
